title: Evaluate tiered cross-encoder candidate pool and upgrade orchestrator for rerank endpoint
creator: Marco Li
description: Problem: Our current cross-encoder rerank endpoint has grown a patchwork of single-family models with inconsistent quality/latency tradeoffs across locales. Upgrades have resulted in surprising regressions for low-volume languages and unpredictable P99 latency spikes during peak batching windows. Goal: Design, evaluate, and implement a tiered candidate pool + orchestrator that lets us safely nominate multiple cross-encoder variants, run locale-aware evaluation gate checks, and perform automated staged rollouts with deterministic rollback triggers. This ticket covers model selection criteria, offline + online regression gating, canary orchestration wiring into Redwood Console, KV warmstart considerations, and a rollout automation runbook.
acceptance_criteria: A documented candidate pool with at least two vetted model families (compact and multilingual) and clear serving-compatibility profiles
Offline eval results (MRR@10, NDCG@10, exact-match delta) for each locale and global summary stored in Drive/Confluence
Defined latency SLOs per tier and verified micro-benchmarks showing no >10% P95 increase vs current baseline for primary locales
Canary harness integrated into Console to route 5%/20%/50% traffic phases with automatic rollback if quality or latency thresholds breached
Automated regression checks (unit + integration) included in CI that block merge if locale-specific model deltas exceed thresholds
Runbook and post-mortem template for any rollout that triggers rollback, with ownership and on-call contacts
testing_plan: Offline: run multilingual eval suites on EvalBench (datasets: RR-2025-multilang-qrels, internal-prod-sampled-100k) producing MRR@10, NDCG@10, and per-locale confidence intervals
Latency bench: per-model tokenized microbench with batch sizes [1,4,8,16] and sequence lengths [64,128,256]; capture P50/P95/P99 and memory footprints
Smoke canary: staged traffic via Console routing (0.5% -> 5% -> 20%) with shadow KV warming for 24h prior to traffic shift
A/B online evaluation using traffic split + metric collection to compute lift and detect drift; tie to alerts in Grafana and DataDog
Regression harness: fuzzed input corpora to catch structured-output breakages and a language coverage checker to ensure minimum sample counts per locale
Performance regression gate: CI job that compares new candidate perf profile against pinned baseline artifacts (artifact store URL in related_links)
rollout_plan: Stage 0 - Nomination: ML selects 2 candidates (compact-crossenc-v2, mce-alpha-multilang) and registers model metadata in catalog
Stage 1 - Offline validation: run full EvalBench; if any locale shows >2% absolute drop in MRR@10, reject candidate
Stage 2 - Shadow + KV warmstart: shadow serve candidate for 24h with KV cache warmstart to prepopulate common prefixes
Stage 3 - Micro-canary (0.5% traffic) for 4h: verify latency SLOs and basic quality signals; automated rollback on latency P95 > baseline*1.2 or quality delta > -1% MRR@10
Stage 4 - Canary expansion (5% -> 20% -> 50%) over 72h with continuous monitoring and manual approval gate at 20%
Stage 5 - Full rollout and deprecate fallbacks once stability observed for 7 days; maintain a fallback mapping in routing policy for 90 days
Rollback triggers: P95 latency > baseline * 1.2 for 30m OR any locale MRR@10 drop > 2% sustained for 15m OR elevated error rate > 0.5%
